title: DC-area forecast: Record warmth possible today; much cooler with showers likely tomorrow
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: A warm start as morning readings rise through the 60s and 70s with plenty of sun. Heating up this afternoon with near-record highs in the mid-80s to near 90, then an evening storm chance.

What’s next? Much cooler temperatures in the 60s on Thursday, then rebounding warmer Friday with a late-day shower and storm threat. A dry weekend starts with a cool and blustery blast of fall on Saturday.

Today’s daily digit — 6/10: Temperatures threaten record highs for the date. Fortunately, October warmth doesn't have the sizzle of midsummer heat. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Wednesday): Mostly sunny as we head for near-record afternoon highs mostly in the mid- to upper 80s, maybe touching 90 in a few hot spots. It's somewhat humid (dew points in the mid- to upper 60s) with light winds from the southwest. An isolated shower is possible by late afternoon. Record highs for the date are 87 at Reagan National, and 86 at both Dulles and BWI. Confidence: Medium-High

Tonight: A few showers or storms are possible during the evening, mainly after 8 p.m., as a cold front comes through. Temperatures stay up in the 70s well into the evening, slipping into the 60s overnight under partly to mostly cloudy skies. Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Thursday): Mostly cloudy with a decent chance of scattered showers at times, and much cooler temperatures holding in the 60s. A morning breeze from the northeast around 10 mph lightens up by afternoon. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow night: A chance of scattered showers continues Thursday night, still with mostly cloudy skies and lows in the upper 50s to low 60s. Confidence: Medium

A look ahead

A brief shower is possible Friday morning, then much of the day should be partly sunny and warm with highs in the upper 70s to low 80s. Showers and thunderstorms are likely at some point midafternoon into evening as a strong cold front comes through. Some storms could produce strong winds. Behind the front, gusty winds blow from the northwest Friday night with lows in the upper 40s to low 50s. Confidence: Low-Medium

The weekend brings a blast of fall. We're partly sunny and windy Saturday, with highs only in the 50s and winds gusting from the northwest around 30 to 40 mph. Winds diminish Saturday night with lows in the upper 30s to low 40s. Sunday trends mostly sunny and not quite as cool, with highs in the upper 50s to low 60s and light winds. Confidence: Medium-High

The early to middle part of next week is looking dry with gradually warmer highs in the 60s to near 70.

DC weather history for October 14

Severe storms in 1995 dumped record rainfall and spawned multiple tornadoes, contributing to one of the wettest Octobers on record.
